story.title: Nepal Flooding Sparks Concerns Over Climate Change Impact on Himalayan Glaciers
story.summary: Recent flooding in Nepal has raised alarms among scientists regarding the accelerating impact of climate change on Himalayan glaciers. While some experts caution against attributing the disaster solely to human-induced climate change, others assert that it exemplifies the catastrophic events they have long predicted. In response to the disaster, India has increased its glacier monitoring efforts to better understand and mitigate the risks posed by rapidly melting glaciers.

timeline_highlights.title: Western Europe Experiences Record Heat in June and July
timeline_highlights.summary: Western Europe has recorded its hottest June and July on record, with average temperatures reaching 21.62°C, surpassing the previous record set in 2022. This extreme heat has been linked to climate change and has resulted in significant drought, wildfires, and health risks across the region. The heat waves began in May and have contributed to a historic summer characterized by severe weather conditions.

event_overview.title: About Climate Change
event_overview.subject: Climate Change
event_overview.summary: Climate change refers to long-term shifts in the climate system, now driven primarily by human greenhouse-gas emissions. It is expressed through changes in average conditions and in the frequency or intensity of some extremes, including heatwaves, heavy precipitation, drought and glacier loss; the developments here are regional examples rather than a single discrete event.

facts.label: Extreme heat
facts.value: The IPCC assesses it as virtually certain that hot extremes, including heatwaves, have become more frequent and more intense across most land regions since the 1950s, with human-caused climate change the main driver.

facts.label: European context
facts.value: Europe is identified by the Copernicus Climate Change Service and the World Meteorological Organization as the fastest-warming continent, warming more than twice as fast as the global average.

facts.label: International policy framework
facts.value: The 2015 Paris Agreement aims to strengthen the global response through mitigation, adaptation and climate-resilient finance, including holding warming well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the cited 2026 heat and Himalayan flooding developments as climate-impact news; it does not attempt to catalogue all climate observations, attribution studies, policies or extreme-weather events worldwide.

related_stories.title: Meta Settles Social Media Addiction Lawsuits for $17 Billion
related_stories.summary: Meta has reached a settlement of up to $17 billion to resolve multistate lawsuits regarding social media addiction. As part of the agreement, the company will implement changes to its platforms, including Facebook and Instagram. The settlement follows extensive negotiations led by state attorneys general amid mounting legal challenges for the tech giant.

related_stories.title: Iceland Votes on Resuming EU Membership Negotiations in Referendum
related_stories.summary: Icelanders are voting in a referendum on whether to resume negotiations for European Union membership. The decision comes after a decade-long suspension of talks, which were halted in 2013 following a shift to a eurosceptic government. The outcome of this referendum is being closely monitored, given its potential implications for Iceland's future relationship with the EU.

related_stories.title: Rescue Efforts Resume in Nepal-Tibet Flood After Initial Halt Due to Lake Overflow
related_stories.summary: Rescue operations have resumed along the Nepal-Tibet border following a temporary halt caused by the risk of new flooding from an overflowing lake. The devastating floods, triggered by a glacial collapse, have resulted in at least 675 confirmed deaths in Nepal and seven in Tibet, with nearly 3,000 people reported missing. Emergency teams are racing to locate over 100 workers trapped in hydropower tunnels and to provide aid to the affected population, which includes 17,000 children in need of assistance.
